title: Basics of Probability

  • Random Experiment: An experiment in which all the possible outcomes are known in advance, but we cannot predict as to which of them will occur when we perform the experiment, e.g.
  • Experiment of tossing a coin is random experiment as the possible outcomes, “Heads” and “Tails” are known in advance, but which one will turn up is not known.

  • We have discussed earlier that P(A) represents the probability of happening event A for which the number of exhaustive cases is the number of elements in the sample space S.

4.7 Independent Events

  • Then, the probability of drawing the second card ‘a card of spades’ given that the first card was spades would be 12/51 and it is the conditional probability.
  • Now, if the first card had been replaced back then this conditional probability would have been 13/52.
  • In the example above, if the next draw is made with replacement, then the draw is not affected by the preceding draws.
